title: Recall the symmetry tests
text: Replace $$(r,\theta)$$ in the equation. If $$(r,-\theta)$$ or $$(-r,\pi-\theta)$$ gives the same equation, the graph is symmetric about the x-axis. If $$(-r,-\theta)$$ or $$(r,\pi-\theta)$$ gives the same equation, it is symmetric about the y-axis. If $$(-r,\theta)$$ or $$(r,\theta+\pi)$$ gives the same equation, it is symmetric about the origin.

title: Apply the tests
text: Replacing θ with $$\theta+\pi$$ gives $$3sin\left(2\theta+2\pi\right)=3sin\left(2\theta\right)$$, so the graph is symmetric about the origin. Replacing $$(r,\theta)$$ with $$(-r,-\theta)$$ gives $$-r=3sin\left(-2\theta\right)$$, which is $$r=3sin\left(2\theta\right)$$ again, so it is symmetric about the y-axis. A graph symmetric about the origin and the y-axis is also symmetric about the x-axis.
